title: Reckoning the Value of a Snowsports School Session the Collective Could Not Run
content:
Where the collective cannot run a Snowsports School session because the mountain is shut, the lifts the session depends on are held, or conditions on the hill make the session unsafe, the school makes good the value of that session as school credit on the booking it was lost from. One credit entry is issued for each session the collective could not run. This note fixes the amount that entry carries.

## The amount

The value of one session is the product's block price divided by the number of sessions the product's block holds. The amount made good is the value of one session taken at the weather share, which stands at 50 percent.

Two further amounts enter the entry. The make-good for the equipment and extras the school had laid on for the participant stands at 0.00 USD. The offset for the household's own days on the mountain stands at 0.00 USD.

The make-good for equipment and extras is added to the amount made good, and the offset for days on the mountain is taken off that combined figure. The credit issued is that result rounded to the nearest cent. Where the offset exceeds the combined figure, no credit is issued at all.

## The same reckoning, step by named step

| Quantity | How it is arrived at |
| --- | --- |
| value of one session | the product's block price divided by the sessions the product's block holds |
| amount made good | the value of one session taken at the weather share of 50 percent |
| make-good for equipment and extras | 0.00 USD |
| offset for days on the mountain | 0.00 USD |
| credit issued | the amount made good, increased by the make-good for equipment and extras and decreased by the offset for days on the mountain, rounded to the nearest cent, and never below nothing |

## A figure worked through on hypothetical inputs

Take a booking of a product whose block price is 900.00 USD and whose block holds 3 sessions, and take one session the collective could not run.

The value of one session is 900.00 USD divided by 3, which is 300.00 USD. The amount made good is 300.00 USD taken at 50 percent, which is 150.00 USD. The make-good for equipment and extras adds 0.00 USD, and the offset for days on the mountain takes off 0.00 USD. The credit issued on that lost session is therefore 150.00 USD.

Had the collective been unable to run two sessions of that same booking, two credit entries would be issued, one for each.

The block prices and the session counts this reckoning reads are published product by product on the Snowsports School tariff.
